summary: Instagram is carrying almost all of the channel's views, while YouTube Shorts is nearly dead for the Hindi videos (most under 25 views). The best videos explain a familiar sensor that people meet in daily life (motion detector, robot avoiding a wall, street light) with a curious 'how does it know?' question, and the top two get real shares and saves. Weak videos are narrower or less visual topics (lift door, tap, smartwatch) with little engagement, and the one English video got YouTube views but no Instagram posting.
winningPattern: Sensor-in-daily-life subject, especially PIR and IR sensors and things that seem to 'see' or 'think' (motion detection, robot avoiding walls, street light sensing dark). Hook is a surprising claim or question in Hinglish ('Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', 'Robot Deewar Se Kaise Bachta Hai?') with a 🤔 emoji and #shorts. Instagram Reels is the platform that delivers (700 to 1400 views); YouTube gives under 25 views on most Hindi videos, so Instagram is the growth engine for now.
doMore: Make more PIR and IR sensor videos from fresh angles, such as robots, security, and things that sense people or obstacles
Open with a bold myth-busting statement before the question, like the PIR title that says the sensor does not see you
Pick topics that show a robot or machine reacting visibly, since the robot video got the most shares (10)
Test the English Arduino-style titles on YouTube again, since the English video got 161 views there versus a Hindi average under 25, and also post it to Instagram
Make a short series from the top videos (part 2 of PIR, IR on a robot) and end each with a question to invite saves and shares
stopDoing: Near-duplicate topics such as two smoke detector videos and two IR videos in one week, which split the audience and drop engagement
Generic or vague 'Kaise Pehchanta Hai' tap and door topics with no visual surprise (the automatic tap video got 2 IG views)
Expecting YouTube to grow from Hindi titles with the same format as Instagram without changing the hook or title
